h: Make a park day of it
p: The Olympic Park is a big place, so think about your route. Stratford station, served by the Central, Jubilee and Elizabeth lines, the DLR and Overground, is the easiest arrival point, and from there it's a walk through Westfield and across the bridges into the park. Allow longer than you expect if you've got little legs with you, and keep an eye on your batting slot so you're not legging it across the park at the last minute.

There's plenty to tie into a session. The ArcelorMittal Orbit, the twisting red sculpture you can't miss, has viewing platforms and a long tunnel slide for those brave enough. The London Aquatics Centre is open for public swimming, so you could squeeze in a dip in the same pool used at the 2012 Games. The London Stadium, home of West Ham, sits in the middle of it all, and Lee Valley VeloPark at the north end lets you have a go on bikes. The playgrounds and water fountains dotted around the park are a godsend for younger kids in summer.

Wear trainers, bring layers, and pack a bottle of water if you're planning a long walk around the park. Batting is thirsty work, and the park's wide open paths are much nicer when you're not overheated. On a sunny day, a picnic on the lawns by the river is a cheap and cheerful way to round off your visit before heading home.
